walkthroughs.body_html:
Component: Listening and Appraising — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component: Listening and Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component: Listening and Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: What three notes form a major triad in root position?
options: Three consecutive scale notes.
Root, major third, perfect fifth.
Any three notes played together.
Very fast.
Very fast.
Any three notes played together.
Slow and sad.
At a walking pace (moderate tempo).

mcqs.q: What happens in the recapitulation of sonata form?
options: The exposition is repeated exactly.
Both subjects return, but the second subject is now in the tonic key.
Any three notes played together.
Entirely new material is introduced.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Note value”?
options: Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dotted note”?
options: Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rest”?
options: Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Semibreve (whole note)”?
options: Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quaver (eighth note)”?
options: Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Filled head with single tail/flag; lasts half a beat in 4/4.
Empty-headed note with no stem; lasts 4 beats in 4/4.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crotchet (quarter note)”?
options: Symbol indicating duration: semibreve, minim, crotchet, quaver, semiquaver.
Dot after note increases its duration by half (e.g., dotted crotchet = 1.5 beats).
Single-flag-less stem with filled head; lasts 1 beat in 4/4.
Symbol indicating silence for a specific duration, mirroring note values.

mcqs.q: How many quavers equal a crotchet?
options: 5 quavers
2 quavers
3 quavers
4 quavers

sequence.def: Begins c.500: monks sing unaccompanied plainchant
c.1600-1750: harpsichord continuo and terraced dynamics
c.1750-1820: elegant balance; the piano replaces the harpsichord
c.1820-1900: rubato, chromatic harmony, huge orchestras
After 1900: serialism, minimalism and electronics arrive
